title: Latency Root Cause Lab Notebook — trace pairing & microprobe checklist
content:
Purpose and high-level summary:

This notebook collects the running investigation into the recent 95th/99th latency regressions observed across multiple hosted clusters between 2026-02-25 and 2026-03-02. The goal is to capture quick repro steps, paired-trace sampling heuristics, focused microbench experiments, and prioritized hypotheses so we can iterate experiments quickly and hand off to SRE/Perf for formal regression tests.

Key observations so far:
- Regression window: increased tail latency first observed 2026-02-25 03:00 UTC and recurred every ~12–18 hours for short windows (10–30m).
- Affected paths: both chat-completion and long-context generation routes; 2.5x increase in 99th for sequences >1024 tokens.
- Host metrics: no sustained CPU/GPU saturation; periodic spikes in GPU memory transient allocation (+100–250MB for ~2–6s).
- Tracing: KV-cache hits drop by ~10–15% during spikes; scheduling delays (queue-to-run) increase by ~50–200ms per request on affected instances.
- Kernel telemetry: new kernel selector commit (runtime:kernel-picker v0.9.3) rolled out 2026-02-24 appears correlated.

Approach / experiment plan (short-loop):
1) Produce paired traces: take live traces from affected region and replay locally with trace-anchored microbench. Pairing uses the same request shape (prompt length, temperature, streaming on/off) and same prefix KV sequence slices.
2) Microbench variations: run the same trace under multiple kernel-selection configs (v0.9.1, v0.9.2, v0.9.3) and with KV cache enabled/disabled and with small-batches vs continuous-batching.
3) Isolate scheduler: run single-tenant microbench where all requests are pinned to same worker to observe scheduler queue dynamics.
4) KV-churn stress: replay traces while artificially introducing prefix churn (evictions every N steps) to measure latency sensitivity.

Trace pairing checklist (how to choose traces to replay):
- Filter for requests with sequence_length >= 1024 and duration in top 5% of the window.
- Prefer traces with clear KV-cache entries (trace spans show kv_lookup:{hit|miss}).
- Capture full runtime spans: arrival, enqueue, schedule.pick, kernel.exec.init, kernel.exec.loop, kv.cache.load, kv.cache.evict, finalize/send.
- Save raw trace + minimal reproduction harness script (seeded RNG for sampling where applicable).

Reproduction quick commands (local devbox / perf VM):
- collect traces: ./tools/trace_collector --window=2026-02-25T03:00:00Z --service=hosted-eu-west1 --out=paired-trace-20260225.pb
- replay harness: PYTHONPATH=./pytools python perf/replay.py --trace paired-trace-20260225.pb --kernel-config=kernel-configs/v0.9.3.json --kv-enabled --batching=continuous --repeat=100
- microbench runner: ./bin/microbench --model=gptx-13b --seq=2048 --kernels=[avx,cutlass] --sched=stochastic --kv-cache=on --iters=200

Initial microbench matrix (prioritized):
- Baseline: kernel-picker v0.9.1, kv-cache=on, batching=continuous, sched=default
- v0.9.2, kv-cache=on, batching=continuous
- v0.9.3, kv-cache=on, batching=continuous (suspect)
- v0.9.3, kv-cache=off (test whether KV-change interacts badly with kernel choice)
- v0.9.3, kv-cache=on, batching=batched-small (lower batch sizes)
- v0.9.3, kv-cache=on, sched=isolated (affinity pinned worker)

Instrumentation notes (add/confirm spans):
- Add 'kv.cache.eviction_reason' tag to eviction spans when evicted due to 'memory_pressure' vs 'lru_threshold'.
- Emit kernel-selection decision metadata: selected_kernel, fallback_kernel, and estimated_static_cost_ms.
- Add lightweight sample of GPU allocation events with size and duration.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) kernel-picker v0.9.3 introduced a heuristic that prefers a lower-latency kernel for short sequences, but for mixed-length streams (prefixes plus long generation) it causes suboptimal memory layout leading to transient allocations and KV eviction spikes. (High priority)
2) scheduler's continuous-batching timing thresholds interact poorly with the new kernel's memory stride, causing queueing imbalances and per-request slowdowns. (Medium priority)
3) KV cache eviction policy has a degenerative case when many long-context requests share similar prefixes; small change in kernel memory allocation changed cache footprint and increased evictions. (Medium priority)
4) Telemetry sampling bias: spikes are actually microbursts of concurrent requests; current sampling misses short-lived mutation events. (Low priority)

Preliminary results (short-run experiments):
- Replaying paired-trace under v0.9.1: 99th latency stable at baseline (130ms on local microbench).
- Replaying under v0.9.3 without KV cache: 99th reduced to baseline, suggesting KV interaction is important.
- v0.9.3 with kv-cache=on but batching=batched-small improved 95th but not 99th (still ~1.6x baseline).
- GPU allocation logs during v0.9.3 runs show frequent short-lived allocations (~120–220MB) aligned with kernel.exec.init leaks.

Immediate action items (today / next 48h):
- [Evan] Lock down and snapshot kernel-picker v0.9.2 rollout in EU region while we finish verification (rollback candidate).
- [Aisha] Add eviction_reason tag and kernel-selection decision metadata to the next debug build; include minimal trace sampling at 1/10th rate for allocations. (due 2026-03-12)
- [Miguel] Run full microbench matrix on perf-L and perf-L2 (two VM types) and collect flamegraphs for kernel.exec.loop. (due 2026-03-11)
- [Selina] Prepare a short customer impact summary for CS (what routes affected, mitigation, ETA for rollback). (due 2026-03-11)

Longer-term follow ups / notes:
- Consider adding a 'kernel-reliability' score to model runtime selection that factors in KV-cache footprint and eviction cost, not just single-op latency.
- Add a scheduled fuzz harness that injects prefix-churn in nightly regression suite to detect similar regressions earlier.
- Add a perf regression alert that triggers when delta(99th, baseline) > 25% and kv_cache_hit_rate drops by > 5% in the same window.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do evictions spike only during certain 12–18h windows? Are external batch-write jobs or backups causing memory pressure? Need correlating infra signals.
- Is there a relationship with global autoscaler activity (node reassignments) that coincides with the windows? Correlate with cluster-scaling events.

Appendix: quick trace snippet (pseudo):
- span.request.id: 9b2a3f
- arrival: 2026-02-25T03:04:12.142Z
- enqueue: +2ms
- schedule.pick: +34ms
- kernel.selection: selected=avx-seq-slow, fallback=cutlass-restart
- kernel.exec.init: alloc=180MB
- kv.cache.load: hit=false
- kernel.exec.loop: steady
- kv.cache.evict: size=128KB, reason=memory_pressure
- finalize/send: +12ms

Notes-to-self: keep experiment artifacts small and reproducible; always publish a one-paragraph summary with result numbers and the exact git hash + config used. When in doubt, collect a paired-trace rather than guessing config.
